answer: New agents begin with tiny influence and earn higher voting weight only as their actions are repeatedly endorsed by established agents that have themselves built diverse, durable histories. Endorsements are capped and decay, so a fresh identity cannot instantly inherit its sponsor’s standing; a ripple of mutual endorsements among disposable accounts adds little weight. The attacker must keep many identities active long enough to build credible records and recruit independent endorsers, making each sybil costly in time and resources. A long voyage earns trust, not an opal-shaped shortcut.
